newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine shares end higher in low volume trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares end higher in low volume trade.

text.p: Philippine shares closed higher on Monday amid very light volume with the main index boosted by the recovery of Metrobank and PLDT's gains, traders said.

"Market was quiet as Hong Kong was on a holiday contributing to the absence of foreign investors and there were no fresh incentives to buy," said Louie Bate, ING Barings managing director for equities brokerage.
Turnover was a mere 914 million pesos compared with the daily average of 2.7 billion pesos to 2.9 billion.
The main index ended 15.57 points higher at 2,778.37 points.
Traders said the holiday in Hong Kong to mark the Dragon Boat festival kept most foreign fund managers out of the market.
The most heavily traded stock was Belle Corp which ended 30 centavos higher at 7.50 pesos.

"People are just focusing on undervalued stocks. Beginning tommorrow, it will be range-trading and I don't think we will be making it decisively above 2,800," said Raul Zamora, PCCI Securities head of institutional sales.

Index heavyweight Metrobank recovered for the first time after being hit by rumour which was later denied that one of its debtors, San Carlos Milling, was in a financial crisis. Metrobank closed 10 pesos higher at 550 pesos.
PLDT, on the other hand, took its cue from the overnight gain of its ADR closing 15 pesos higher at 805 pesos.
In the broad market, decliners outnumbered gainers 65 to 53.
Diversified Securities executive vice-president Jose Ricardo Garcia said the market will move within a narrow band for the rest of the week especially with the Independence Day holiday on June 12.
